title: How do you know Trent is lawful, or papal acts uncorrupted?
source_text: XVIII. Nos igitur jure quoque Pontificios rogare possumus, Unde scitis hoc vel illud Concilium legitimum esse, & Pontificem istum non esse intrusum, & vitio creatum, sicut multos alios, quorum successores acta resciderunt, & memoriam infamarunt? Quo certo argumento probare potestis Concilium Tridentinum vere fuisse in Christi nomine congregatum? An quia ipsum hoc dicit? Sed idem sibi ipsi fidem facere non potest, & seipsum probare: suntque alia multa impia Concilia quae se itidem duci Spiritu sancto jactant. An quia Papa Romanus Concilium istud approbavit? Sed approbavit quoque illud Lateranense, cujus tamen authoritate Pontificii omnes sese obstringi nolunt. Deinde quo certo fidei argumento probari potest Pontifices illos, qui Concilia probarunt, legitimos fuisse, neque per vim & simoniace occupasse sedem suam? Saltem enim hac de re major certitudo haberi non potest quam historica & moralis quae ad fidem non sufficit. Praeterea quomodo fides alicui fiet exemplaria Conciliorum atque Decretorum Pontificalium corrupta non esse, neque iis quicquam additum aut detractum, cum certum sit multa decreta Pontificibus afficta fuisse, & plurimorum Conciliorum acta corrupta atque depravata? Nec dubitationem hanc tollet nova Pontificis aut Concilii alicujus declaratio. Nam adversus hoc postremum Concilium eaedem quae adversus prius difficultates movebuntur, & sic in infinitum. Itaque, si locum habet Pontificiorum ratio adversus Scripturae sacrae certitudinem & authoritatem, evertetur quoque Ecclesiae & Conciliorum atque Pontificum authoritas: nec ullum supererit fidei fundamentum.
pass_a_gloss: We therefore can also by right ask the Pontificians: Whence do you know that this or that Council is lawful, and that that Pontiff is not an intruder and created by defect, like many others whose successors rescinded their acts and branded their memory? By what certain argument can you prove that the Council of Trent was truly gathered in Christ's name? Because it itself says so? But the same cannot make faith for itself and prove itself; and there are many other impious Councils that likewise boast that they are led by the Holy Spirit. Because the Roman Pope approved that Council? But he also approved that Lateran one, by whose authority yet not all Pontificians are willing to bind themselves. Next, by what certain argument of faith can it be proved that those Pontiffs who approved Councils were lawful, and did not occupy their seat by force and simoniacally? For at least about this matter no greater certainty can be had than historical and moral, which does not suffice for faith. Besides, how will anyone have faith that the copies of Councils and Pontifical Decrees are not corrupted, and that nothing has been added to them or taken away, when it is certain that many decrees have been fastened upon Pontiffs, and the acts of very many Councils corrupted and depraved? Nor will a new declaration of some Pontiff or Council remove this doubt. For against this latest Council the same difficulties will be moved that were moved against the earlier one, and so to infinity. Therefore, if the Pontificians' reasoning against the certainty and authority of sacred Scripture has place, the authority of the Church and of Councils and of Pontiffs will also be overturned; and no foundation of faith will remain.
pass_b_english: We may fairly ask them in turn: how do you know this or that council is lawful, or that this pope is not an intruder created by defect — like many others whose successors cancelled their acts and stained their memory?

By what certain argument do you prove Trent was truly gathered in Christ's name? Because it says so? Nothing proves itself; and many wicked councils have boasted the same Spirit. Because the Roman pope approved it? He also approved that Lateran whose authority not all Romanists will bind themselves to.

By what certain argument of faith can you prove the approving popes were lawful and did not seize the see by force or simony? At best you have historical and moral certainty, which does not suffice for faith.

How will anyone trust that copies of councils and papal decrees are uncorrupted, with nothing added or cut, when it is certain many decrees were fastened on popes and many councils' acts corrupted and spoiled?
A fresh papal or conciliar declaration will not end the doubt: the same difficulties rise against the latest council as against the earlier one, and so without end.
If their case against Scripture's certainty and authority stands, the authority of church, councils, and popes falls with it — and no foundation of faith is left.

lemmas.gloss: to make faith for itself / prove itself
